reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a TRX crypto arbitrage method with unusually fast profit claims, including 9 percent in 15 minutes, $500 in 15 minutes, and over $1,500 from one round. It ties those claims to a concrete participation flow involving buying TRX on Binance, transferring it through Bitqlux/BitClucks-style exchange screens, selling it for USDT, and withdrawing funds. The evidence does not verify the exchange rates, account ownership, completed profits, or transaction outcomes.

citations.quote: How To Make Money Through Tron Arbitrage Using the BitClucks.com Exchange
earn 9 percent in 15 minutes just by watching the video to the end.
we buy TRX on Binance for $ 5.000 and make a deposit on the Bitqlux exchange, then change the TRX to usdt and withdraw.
The Tron exchange rate on this platform is 10% higher than on Binance. Go to the Wallet and click on Deposit. Select Tron and click Show Address. Copy the address and go to Binance.
I will start with an amount of $100,000 TRX but you can deposit any amount.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker describes a method and leaves the amount to the viewer: “you can deposit any amount.” That is a meaningful limit on how prescriptive the demonstration is. The claimed rate difference is presented as a rate “on this platform,” not as a promise that every viewer will receive the same result. The profit claims deserve scrutiny, but the supplied material does not establish that the speaker guarantees a return on each viewer’s transaction.

citations.quote: I will start with an amount of $100,000 TRX but you can deposit any amount.
The Tron exchange rate on this platform is 10% higher than on Binance.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution rightly identifies striking profit claims, but its own quoted workflow describes buying, exchanging and withdrawing, not an explicit promise that a viewer’s deposit will earn a fixed return. Nor does the absence of verification establish that the narrated result is false. Those are reasons to question the claim, not proof of deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: we buy TRX on Binance for $ 5.000 and make a deposit on the Bitqlux exchange, then change the TRX to usdt and withdraw.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Choice of deposit size is not a risk warning. The description explicitly invites viewers to watch to learn how to earn 9 percent in 15 minutes, then claims $500 earned in that period. Coupled with directions to deposit on the named exchange, the earnings pitch is more consequential than the absence of the word “guarantee.”

citations.quote: I will show you how to earn 9 percent in 15 minutes just by watching the video to the end.
Total we earned $500 for only 15 minutes.
make a deposit on the Bitqlux exchange

opening.argument: Judge, the video can be read as an operational walkthrough of an arbitrage trade. The narration takes viewers through selecting Tron, obtaining a deposit address, navigating to spot trading and selling, then opening the withdrawal flow. The sampled trading screen shows a Sell TRX control. That sequence supports a tutorial reading: it shows what the speaker says they did and which controls they used. The claimed earnings should not be treated as independently verified, but an unverified demonstration is not, by itself, evidence that the creator controls the exchange or that viewers’ funds are lost.

citations.quote: Go to the Wallet and click on Deposit. Select Tron and click Show Address. Copy the address and go to Binance.
Now after the funds have been credited to the balance, navigate to the Spot trading section and sell Olivertron.
Go to the Wallet section and click on the Withdraw button

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the exchange instructions as a participation flow. They are also precisely the steps an arbitrage tutorial would need to explain. Its concern that profits and withdrawals are unverified is fair, but the visible trading control establishes only an interface, while the narration describes a process; neither resolves whether the speaker’s reported round succeeded.

citations.quote: navigate to the Spot trading section and sell Olivertron.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is also the mechanism by which viewers are directed to transfer crypto to the promoted exchange. The description does more than explain controls: it promises to show viewers how to earn 9 percent in 15 minutes and claims a completed $500 gain. The trading interface does not verify a completed, profitable withdrawal.

citations.quote: I will show you how to earn 9 percent in 15 minutes just by watching the video to the end.
we buy TRX on Binance for $ 5.000 and make a deposit on the Bitqlux exchange, then change the TRX to usdt and withdraw. Total we earned $500 for only 15 minutes.

opening.argument: Judge, the described activity is buying one cryptoasset, selling it in a spot market and withdrawing the proceeds. The description supplies separate links for buying and selling; the narration points to wallet and trading controls. The supplied material does not show a request for credentials, a recruitment chain or a contract promising periodic payouts. It does instruct a deposit, so the transfer deserves caution, but a deposit used in an exchange trade is not alone proof that the destination is fraudulent. Assess the earnings claim critically without treating every described trading step as a demonstrated scam mechanism.

citations.quote: Buy crypto - https://www.binance.com/ Sell crypto - https://bitqlux.com/
Go to the Wallet and click on Deposit. Select Tron and click Show Address.
navigate to the Spot trading section and sell Olivertron.
Go to the Wallet section and click on the Withdraw button

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution points to the large, fast returns and the named exchange. Those points justify skepticism, but the quoted procedure describes a trade followed by withdrawal, not a stated requirement to lock funds or recruit others. A screen or narration cannot verify a successful payout; equally, that verification gap does not identify where any viewer’s money went.

citations.quote: then change the TRX to usdt and withdraw.
Go to the Wallet section and click on the Withdraw button

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Credentials, recruitment and locked funds are not necessary to understand the concern here. The creator directs viewers to deposit crypto on a named exchange while claiming unusually rapid gains from doing so. The supplied interface does not verify the quoted rate advantage or the claimed profit, and a withdrawal instruction is not evidence that a withdrawal completed.
